title: UI: Make TagsFilter state persistent
body:
Closes #32986

## What I did

* Moved TagsFilter state for currently selected filters from the TagsFilter & Sidebar components into the `layout` module
* Made that state persistent
* Moved UI-related state (filter count, grouping of filters) to TagsFilterPanel where it is actually consumed
* Mockied the `layout` module for TagsFilter* stories

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Class component approach is reasonable for coordinating store and React state.**

The MockAPIWrapper correctly bridges the testing store with React's component lifecycle. However, there's a potential issue:

**Potential state assignment issue on line 90**: `this.state` is assigned directly in the constructor, but it's not used as React component state. This is confusing because React class components use `this.state` for managed state. Since you're using `this.setState(newState)` in the store callback (line 48), React expects `this.state` to be initialized properly for the component's state management.



<details>
<summary>🔎 Suggested fix: Rename to avoid confusion with React's this.state</summary>

```diff
-    this.api = api as API;
-    this.state = this.store.getState();
+    this.api = api as API;
+    // Note: We don't need to store this as the store already holds the state
+    // and the component re-renders via setState callback in the store onChange
```

Alternatively, if you need the initial state for reference, use a different property name:

```diff
-    this.state = this.store.getState();
+    this.initialStoreState = this.store.getState();
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/TagsFilter.stories.tsx around lines
22 to 91, avoid assigning to React's this.state directly in the constructor;
instead rename that property to something non-React like this.storeState and
initialize it from the testing store (this.storeState = this.store.getState());
remove the direct this.state assignment, keep the existing
this.setState(newState) store callback for React updates, and update any
downstream references to use this.storeState.
```

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Testing store can still read persisted state via `getInitialState`.**

`createTestingStore` disables writes, but `Store.getInitialState()` always merges local/session storage. That can leak prior browser state into stories/tests, which defeats the “in-memory store” intent. Consider skipping reads when `upstreamPersistence` is false.  


<details>
<summary>🛠️ Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
  getInitialState(base: State) {
+   if (!this.upstreamPersistence) {
+     return { ...base };
+   }
    return { ...base, ...get(store.local), ...get(store.session) };
  }
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/core/src/manager-api/store.ts` around lines 126 - 159,
createTestingStore currently disables writes via upstream.allowPersistence=false
but Store.getInitialState still merges from local/session storage; update the
contract so getInitialState honors the upstream persistence flag: modify
Store.getInitialState (or the Store constructor initialization) to check
upstream.allowPersistence (or upstreamPersistence) and skip reading/merging from
localStorage/sessionStorage when that flag is falsy, or alternatively have
createTestingStore pass an explicit upstream property (e.g., allowPersistence:
false or a no-op read function) that signals Store to avoid persisting reads so
the testing store remains purely in-memory.
```

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Select‑all should ignore hidden built‑in filters.**

Built‑ins with `count === 0` are hidden, but `setAllFilters` still includes them. In projects without docs/play/test, “Select all” can filter out every story unexpectedly.  

<details>
<summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  const setAllFilters = useCallback(
-    (selected: boolean) => {
-      api.setAllTagFilters(selected ? Object.keys(filtersById) : [], []);
-    },
-    [api, filtersById]
-  );
+  const setAllFilters = useCallback(
+    (selected: boolean) => {
+      const selectableIds = Object.values(filtersById)
+        .filter((filter) => filter.type !== 'built-in' || filter.count > 0)
+        .map((filter) => filter.id);
+      api.setAllTagFilters(selected ? selectableIds : [], []);
+    },
+    [api, filtersById]
+  );
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@code/core/src/manager/components/sidebar/TagsFilterPanel.tsx` around lines
142 - 146, setAllFilters currently passes all tag ids from
Object.keys(filtersById) to api.setAllTagFilters, which erroneously includes
hidden built‑in filters (those with count === 0); update setAllFilters so when
selected is true it builds the id list by iterating filtersById and excluding
filters where filter.builtIn (or builtin) is true AND filter.count === 0, then
pass that filtered id array to api.setAllTagFilters (leave the else branch as
[]). Reference: setAllFilters, filtersById, api.setAllTagFilters, and the filter
objects' count and built‑in flag.
```

</details>

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
I suggest we add the data to the state and pass it down from a container component instead of adding a new getter method.

That way, the UI is responsive to the state changes.

As implemented, if this component is memoized, it will not re-render unless either changes: 
- `api` (will never change)
- `indexJson` (will likely change as a result of the filters-change) 

My advice is to avoid using/creating state-getter functions, as we will end up depending on accidental re-render.
And thus introduce state bugs when we fix those accidental re-renders.
